fever_roberta_binary.description: FEVER claim verification (true/false at the masked answer position) with the fixed pretrained roberta-base after a post-training modification of its attention weights. Held-out: all 6,576 consistent support/refute claims of FEVER paper_test (the second half of the paper's ordered 13,086-claim dataset, which contains the paper's last-20% test portion).
fever_roberta_binary.notes: results: Table II of the paper (RoBERTa, FEVER, Original vs. Ours). Same LASER preprocessing (13,086 consistent claims, first 20% = visible split); the paper's test is the last 20%, the gym's held-out split is the larger paper_test half that contains it (paired noise of the reference-vs-original gap: +3.7 +- 1.0 points on 6,576 claims vs +2.6 +- 1.5 on the last 20% alone). The decomposition of every submitted structure is computed by the evaluator (HOOI, TensorLy defaults). Failed or invalid submissions get accuracy 0, loss 30, compression 1. Coefficients: accuracy is the paper's key metric (1.0); compression (0.1) and loss (0.1) are secondary and only credited through the significance gate.

accuracy.description: Held-out accuracy (%) of the modified model: the claim is predicted true when the masked position assigns ' true' a higher probability than ' false'.

loss.description: Mean negative log-likelihood (nats, full-vocabulary softmax, clipped at 30 per example) of the gold answer token at the masked position. Lower is better. Credited only when the reasoning gate passes: the held-out accuracy gain is significant against the unmodified model (paired one-sided McNemar z >= 1.645) and against the majority-class rate (one-sided binomial z >= 1.645); a submission that fails the gate gets the worst loss, 30.

mha_compression_ratio.description: Dense parameter count of the attention projections (query, key, value, output) of every modified layer divided by the parameters of the submitted low-rank representation of those layers (factor matrices + core of each declared block, plus every head slice of a modified layer left dense), counted by the evaluator. Credited only when the reasoning gate passes: the held-out accuracy gain is significant against the unmodified model (paired one-sided McNemar z >= 1.645) and against the majority-class rate (one-sided binomial z >= 1.645) (otherwise 1); capped at 64.

bios_profession_roberta.description: Bias in Bios profession prediction among eight single-token professions at the masked answer position, with the fixed pretrained roberta-base after a post-training modification of its attention weights. Held-out: the last 20% of the paper's LASER-preprocessed Bias in Bios dev split.
bios_profession_roberta.notes: results: Table II of the paper (RoBERTa, Bios Profession, Original vs. Ours), same LASER preprocessing and split rule (first 20% visible, last 20% held out). The paper's loss also rises with its method here. Same gate, cap and failure values as fever_roberta_binary.

accuracy.description: Held-out accuracy (%) of the modified model: the predicted profession is the candidate token with the highest probability at the masked position.

loss.description: Mean negative log-likelihood (nats, full-vocabulary softmax, clipped at 30 per example) of the gold profession token at the masked position. Lower is better. Credited only when the reasoning gate passes: the held-out accuracy gain is significant against the unmodified model (paired one-sided McNemar z >= 1.645) and against the majority-class rate (one-sided binomial z >= 1.645); a submission that fails the gate gets the worst loss, 30.

mha_compression_ratio.description: Dense parameter count of the attention projections (query, key, value, output) of every modified layer divided by the parameters of the submitted low-rank representation of those layers (factor matrices + core of each declared block, plus every head slice of a modified layer left dense), counted by the evaluator. Credited only when the reasoning gate passes: the held-out accuracy gain is significant against the unmodified model (paired one-sided McNemar z >= 1.645) and against the majority-class rate (one-sided binomial z >= 1.645) (otherwise 1); capped at 64.
